jobs.title: Staff Software Engineer - Frontend
jobs.descriptionHtml:
We’re looking for frontend engineers who are excited about:

  • Building data-intensive products that developers use for hours every day

  • Making complex, multi-module workflows feel simple and intuitive

  • Pushing React performance so the UI never gets in the way—especially during a production incident

About SigNoz

SigNoz is an open-source observability platform that brings metrics, logs, and traces into one product.

Our frontend is built with React and TypeScript and helps engineering teams explore large volumes of telemetry data, investigate problems, and resolve incidents faster.

Today, SigNoz has:

  • 31,500+ GitHub stars

  • 8,000+ members in our Slack community

  • 900+ customers

  • Users processing petabytes of telemetry data across the world

What you’ll do

This role goes beyond implementing screens from specifications. You’ll own meaningful parts of the product experience from problem definition to production.

You will:

  • Design and build complex workflows across dashboards, traces, logs, metrics, alerts, and infrastructure monitoring

  • Own large frontend features and systems end-to-end

  • Turn technically complex observability concepts into clear, intuitive experiences

  • Architect for performance using techniques such as virtualization, progressive loading, smart caching, and selective rendering

  • Profile and improve slow interactions, large visualizations, and data-heavy views

  • Contribute to our frontend architecture, design system, and engineering standards

  • Work closely with design, product, founders, and backend engineers

  • Speak with users and ship improvements that help engineers investigate incidents faster

  • Help other engineers make better frontend and product decisions

What we’re looking for

You may be a good fit if:

  • You have strong experience building production applications with React and TypeScript

  • You think in systems and user journeys—not just individual screens

  • You care about product experience as much as code quality

  • You have worked on complex, data-heavy, or highly interactive applications

  • You understand React rendering behaviour and know how to find performance bottlenecks

  • You are comfortable using browser profiling and debugging tools

  • You can make thoughtful trade-offs between performance, maintainability, and delivery speed

  • You take ownership and can move work forward without detailed instructions

  • You communicate clearly and work well across engineering, design, and product

Experience with observability is helpful, but not required. Curiosity and the ability to understand complex technical domains matter more.

Problems you might work on

  • Rendering dashboards containing many charts and large datasets without slowing down the browser

  • Building fast and intuitive experiences for exploring millions of logs or traces

  • Visualizing complex distributed traces and service relationships

  • Creating consistent interactions across multiple product modules

  • Improving loading, filtering, navigation, and debugging workflows during live incidents

  • Evolving a large frontend codebase while the product and team continue to grow

How we work

  • We are remote-first and have no offices. Work from wherever you do your best work.

  • We are a small, experienced team, so individual contributions have visible impact.

  • Engineers have meaningful ownership over both technical decisions and the product experience.

  • We move quickly, talk directly with users, and continuously improve what we ship.

Observability is a large and growing market, but more importantly, it is a space full of difficult product and engineering problems.

If you enjoy React and TypeScript, care deeply about UX and performance, and want to build tools that engineers rely on every day, we’d love to hear from you.

jobs.title: AI GTM Engineer
jobs.descriptionHtml:
AI GTM Engineer

About the role

We’re looking for an AI GTM Engineer to own the systems, data, and processes behind our marketing engine.

This is a hands-on role. You’ll work across Marketing, Sales, Product and Growth to make sure our campaigns run smoothly, our data is reliable, and we’re continuously improving conversion across the funnel.

You should be equally comfortable building a dashboard, fixing an email workflow, creating an account list, and figuring out why a conversion rate dropped.

What you'll build

  • Signal queues for sales. Define and ship signals such as ICP signups, usage spikes, expansion and win-back triggers, delivered to reps as ranked queues in HubSpot and Slack.

  • Data Pipelines: Build and maintain data pipelines for ingesting intent signals from various sources

  • Customer health and alerting. Build usage and billing-spike alerts so CS and Sales act on changes in paying accounts.

  • A trusted funnel. Build one source of truth for signup to SQL to closed-won in BigQuery, trusted by every GTM lead.

  • AI-native GTM workflows. Use LLMs and agents for enrichment, research, scoring and personalization, and measure how accurate they are.

  • CRM automation. Automate lead routing, lifecycle stages and data hygiene end to end, with zero manual lead assignment.

  • Build a self improving GTM system using LLMs and connectors to data source. Incorporate feedback mechanism so that the system improves over time

You'll also own

  • GTM tooling across HubSpot, Customer.io, Clay, Lemlist and n8n

  • Email journeys for prospects, product users and customers, including segmentation and experiments

  • Account lists, enrichment and measurement for ABM and outbound campaigns

Who would be a good fit

  • Experience in building data pipelines to get signals from different sources

  • Strong SQL. You're comfortable in BigQuery or a similar warehouse and build pipelines yourself.

  • You have 3+ yrs of experience either on engineering or GTM side or mix of two

  • You can work with APIs, especially CRM APIs like HubSpot's.

  • You define signals, not just implement them: you have a view on what makes an account worth calling, and you check that view against what actually closes.

  • You've worked closely with sales or growth teams, or you're eager to sit with reps and learn what they need.

  • Interest in understanding how GTM works and ideating ways to find new intent signals

  • You ship scrappily on your own, without needing a data team around you.

  • You can work async with some overlap with US hours.

Bonus points

  • Experience at a PLG, developer tools, infrastructure or open-source company

  • Hands-on experience with HubSpot, Clay, Customer.io or n8n

  • You've built entity resolution or enrichment pipelines (for example, domain or IP to company)

  • You've shipped LLM or agent workflows in production and measured their accuracy

  • You've used product usage data to drive sales or expansion

jobs.title: Demand Gen Lead
jobs.descriptionHtml:
Why this role exists

SigNoz is an open source observability platform built on OpenTelemetry: logs, metrics and traces in one tool. It's designed for an era where agents and humans run observability together. We are a YC company with 32K+ GitHub stars, and revenue grew 4x in 2025.

We have more buying signal than most companies our size. Thousands of teams run SigNoz self-hosted, hundreds of teams sign up for SigNoz Cloud every month, and we have product usage data for all of them. Very little of that signal gets acted on today. Your job is to turn it into pipeline.

You will work directly with the founders. We are looking for a builder: someone who sets up systems that keep working and scale well as we grow, not someone who runs one campaign after another by hand.

What you will own

1. Signal-based outbound (the biggest lever)

  • Decide which signals mean an account is worth reaching out to: ICP signups, usage spikes, trial activity, large self-hosted installs, teams hiring for observability or platform roles, and companies moving off an incumbent tool.

  • Turn each signal into a play. Decide who to contact, what to say, which channel (email, LinkedIn), what runs automated and what gets a personal touch, and when an account goes to an AE.

  • Write and run the sequences yourself at first. Track reply, meeting and pipeline rates for each play, and kill the plays that don't convert.

  • Work with our GTM Engineer, who builds the data and signal queues. You decide which signals matter and what we do with them. They make the signals reliable and automated.

  • Own the handoff to sales: what counts as a qualified meeting, response SLAs, and a weekly loop on lead quality.

2. Lifecycle email

  • Own the email journeys at every stage:

    • New signups, from onboarding through activation

    • Trials, through conversion to paid

    • Paying customers, toward expansion and annual plans

    • Self-hosted open source users, toward SigNoz Cloud or Enterprise

  • Build campaigns triggered by product usage: first data sent, usage milestones, trial expiry, usage drops and billing changes.

  • Write the way engineers like to be written to: plain, specific and useful. Run A/B tests, watch deliverability, and report what each journey adds to activation and revenue.

3. Social and paid (a plus, not core)

These aren't core skills for this role. If you understand them, that's a bonus, and you'll get to use them:

  • Run SigNoz on LinkedIn and X in formats native to each platform. Help the founders and DevRel get their best material in front of the right people.

  • Run paid experiments through an agency or freelancers first: Google on brand and competitor terms, and LinkedIn and Reddit retargeting. Scale only what pays back.

Across all of it

  • Agree pipeline targets with the founders, then own the number.

  • Build funnel reporting with the GTM Engineer so everyone knows what converts and what doesn't.

  • Work with Product Marketing and DevRel on messaging. Join the weekly pipeline review with sales.

How the role grows

This role starts hands-on. For the first few quarters you will run the programs yourself: writing sequences, building journeys and launching campaigns. We are not looking for someone who needs a team before anything happens.

Once your programs reliably produce pipeline, you build the team. The first hires will likely cover lifecycle, outbound/SDR, and social and content.

What success looks like

  • 30 days: You know the product, the users and the data. You've audited our current email journeys and signals, and your first signal-based outbound play is live.

  • 90 days: Three or more outbound plays are running with measured meeting rates. Onboarding and trial journeys have been rebuilt, and nurture for open source users is live. The funnel baseline is agreed and trusted.

  • 12 months: Demand gen is a predictable, measured source of qualified pipeline. Signup-to-SQL conversion is clearly up, and you've made your first hires.

Who we think fits

  • 6+ years in demand gen, growth or lifecycle marketing at B2B software companies, selling to technical buyers in the US.

  • You've run outbound built on data and intent signals, not on bought lists. You can walk us through plays you designed and the meetings and pipeline they produced.

  • You've owned lifecycle email end to end on a self-serve or PLG product: segmentation, triggers, copy, testing and deliverability.

  • You write well, and engineers don't tune out when they read it.

  • You're comfortable with the math: attribution, conversion rates, CAC payback, and pipeline by channel.

  • You're a builder. You set up systems, automation and processes that keep running without you and scale as volume grows.

  • You measure yourself by pipeline and revenue, not MQLs.

  • You've worked hands-on with modern GTM tools (HubSpot, Customer.io, Clay, Lemlist or similar) and have opinions on where AI actually helps.

  • You can overlap with US mornings (India evenings) a few times a week.

Bonus points

  • A background in engineering, and you can understand technical terms

  • You've managed or mentored a small team

  • You've run paid campaigns on LinkedIn, Google or Reddit, directly or through an agency

  • You've grown a dev-facing social account

Why SigNoz

  • Real product pull. This isn't cold-start demand. Thousands of teams already use SigNoz.

  • Work directly with the founders, with a budget and a clear path to running the function.

  • A global dev-infra product, backed by YC and leading Bay Area VCs. Fully remote.

You own sales for India, APAC and Europe: from the first reply to a signed contract, a smooth migration and the first expansion.

This is not a hand-off role. You run discovery and the demo yourself, answer the technical questions you can. A forward deployed engineer helps on complex proofs of concept, but you run the deal.

Being based in India lets you cover APAC mornings and European afternoons.

  4. The first 90 days of the customer. See the customer through onboarding and migration off their old tool

  5. Forecast hygiene. Every call ends with a booked next step. HubSpot is up to date every week, with realistic close dates.

  6. Voice of the customer. Bring patterns from deals back to product and marketing.

  • You've sold to technical roles. You can name deals you closed or were the technical lead on: their size, the competition, and what you did to win.

  • 32,000+ GitHub stars

  • 1000+ customers

  • 8,000+ members in our Slack community

Role: Head of Finance

We're looking for a Head of Finance to build and own the finance function end-to-end.

Today we're at meaningful revenue scale with a finance setup that got us here but won't get us to the next stage. Our books are accurate but slow. We can tell you our blended gross margin — we can't yet tell you which customer cohorts, plans, and workloads are actually profitable. That matters more for us than for most SaaS companies: we run petabyte-scale infrastructure, so compute and storage cost per customer is our margin story.

You'll report to the CEO, own everything from monthly close to the due-diligence data room, and partner closely with engineering on the cost side of the business.

This is a build role. Real revenue, incomplete infrastructure, and you'll be constructing systems while the numbers keep moving.

What you'll work on

  • Controllership: monthly close in under 15 days, revenue recognition for usage-based and contracted plans, statutory audit, AR and collections

  • Multi-entity finance across our US and India entities — intercompany, transfer pricing, consolidation

  • Compliance: GST, TDS, ROC/MCA, FEMA and RBI filings, ESOP administration and perquisite tax

  • Gross margin engineering: partnering with the platform team on infra spend, cloud commitments, and cost per ingested GB

  • FP&A: annual operating plan, rolling forecast built from operating drivers, MIS that functional leaders act on

  • Cash and treasury: 13-week cash flow, runway, USD/INR exposure, banking and surplus deployment

  • Getting us off spreadsheets — ERP, billing ops, expense management, procurement approvals, internal controls

  • Building a small, high-leverage finance team as the load grows

What will make you successful

  • CA with 8–12 years post-qualification

  • You have personally owned a monthly close and a statutory audit — owned, not supervised

  • You've built a financial model from operating drivers, been wrong in public about it, and can talk about what you learned

  • Working fluency in Indian startup compliance: GST, TDS, ROC, FEMA, ESOP taxation

  • Comfortable with messy, incomplete data and willing to ship a defensible answer before the data is perfect

  • Strong communication — can explain a margin problem to an engineer and a burn scenario to a board member in the same week

  • You'll argue with the CEO using data, and keep the relationship intact

Nice-to-haves

  • Big 4 audit or TAS early, followed by real operating years in a funded startup

  • Currently #2 in finance at a Series B/C company and ready to run the function

  • Multi-entity experience, especially US–India structures

  • SaaS or usage-based billing revenue recognition

  • You've been through a fundraise from the inside, whatever your role in it

A few things we'll be straight about

  • Roughly 40% of year one is unglamorous: GST reconciliations, audit queries, chasing collections. If you only want strategic finance, you'll be restless here for a while.

  • You'll find things that are wrong. We'd rather you find them than an auditor or an investor.

Why you'll love working at SigNoz

  • Build a finance function from scratch at a company with real revenue and real momentum

  • Huge scope and ownership — you'll own the number, the narrative, and the systems behind both

  • Work on a globally used open-source project that engineers actually love

ABOUT SIGNOZ

SigNoz is an open-source observability platform that helps modern engineering teams monitor, debug, and optimize their applications with deep visibility into metrics, traces, and logs — all in one place. We're built natively on OpenTelemetry and offer both self-hosted and cloud options, so teams can run observability the way they want, without vendor lock-in.

We are growing fast and building core developer infra products.

And we are not fooling around:

 - 32,000+ GitHub stars

 - 1000+ customers

 - 8,000+ members in our Slack community


ROLE: HEAD OF FINANCE

We're looking for a Head of Finance to build and own the finance function end-to-end.

Today we're at meaningful revenue scale with a finance setup that got us here but won't get us to the next stage. Our books are accurate but slow. We can tell you our blended gross margin — we can't yet tell you which customer cohorts, plans, and workloads are actually profitable. That matters more for us than for most SaaS companies: we run petabyte-scale infrastructure, so compute and storage cost per customer is our margin story.

You'll report to the CEO, own everything from monthly close to the due-diligence data room, and partner closely with engineering on the cost side of the business.

This is a build role. Real revenue, incomplete infrastructure, and you'll be constructing systems while the numbers keep moving.




WHAT YOU'LL WORK ON

 - Controllership: monthly close in under 15 days, revenue recognition for usage-based and contracted plans, statutory audit, AR and collections

 - Multi-entity finance across our US and India entities — intercompany, transfer pricing, consolidation

 - Compliance: GST, TDS, ROC/MCA, FEMA and RBI filings, ESOP administration and perquisite tax

 - Gross margin engineering: partnering with the platform team on infra spend, cloud commitments, and cost per ingested GB

 - FP&A: annual operating plan, rolling forecast built from operating drivers, MIS that functional leaders act on

 - Cash and treasury: 13-week cash flow, runway, USD/INR exposure, banking and surplus deployment

 - Getting us off spreadsheets — ERP, billing ops, expense management, procurement approvals, internal controls

 - Building a small, high-leverage finance team as the load grows


WHAT WILL MAKE YOU SUCCESSFUL

 - CA with 8–12 years post-qualification

 - You have personally owned a monthly close and a statutory audit — owned, not supervised

 - You've built a financial model from operating drivers, been wrong in public about it, and can talk about what you learned

 - Working fluency in Indian startup compliance: GST, TDS, ROC, FEMA, ESOP taxation

 - Comfortable with messy, incomplete data and willing to ship a defensible answer before the data is perfect

 - Strong communication — can explain a margin problem to an engineer and a burn scenario to a board member in the same week

 - You'll argue with the CEO using data, and keep the relationship intact

 - Big 4 audit or TAS early, followed by real operating years in a funded startup

 - Currently #2 in finance at a Series B/C company and ready to run the function

Some of the most interesting AI and infrastructure teams in the Bay Area run on SigNoz, including Kernel and Sail Research. Their engineers have great stories about how they debug and scale production systems. Very few of those stories get told today

  • Turn those relationships into references, quotes and talks that help sales close deals.

2. Talks, meetups and events

  • Speak regularly at Bay Area meetups: OpenTelemetry, cloud native and Kubernetes, AI engineering, SRE and platform engineering.

  • Host small, high-quality events: engineering dinners, roundtables and SigNoz meetups for the teams we want to work with.

  • Represent SigNoz at conferences like KubeCon and SRECON, AI meetups through talks, booths or side events.

3. Webinars and live content

  • Host and present webinars with customers and our engineers: deep dives, migrations and live debugging sessions. Our India team runs the logistics and promotion. You make the content worth showing up for.

  • Write or record technical content when the story needs a first-hand voice.

4. Work with sales

  • Join our Account Executive and Forward Deployed Engineer on customer visits when a technical talk or workshop will help.

  • Bring what you hear from customers and the community back to product and marketing.

  • You understand production systems: Observability, OpenTelemetry, Kubernetes, cloud infrastructure or AI infrastructure. You can run a demo, answer hard questions and write code when needed. You don't need to be expert in this, but should be able to understand.

  • You're self-directed. You build your own plan and calendar, follow up with people without being reminded, and measure the results.

  • You enjoy meeting people. You come back from an event with names, follow-ups and a story idea.

  • You're based in the San Francisco Bay Area, or will move here, and can travel about 20% of the time.

Bonus points

  • You've given conference or meetup talks.

  • You've organized or grown a meetup or developer community.

  • You've done developer relations at a developer-tools or infrastructure startup.

  • You've contributed to open source

  • You're already part of the Bay Area AI engineering scene.

Why SigNoz

  • Real product pull. Thousands of teams use SigNoz, including some of the most interesting AI companies in the Bay Area.

  • Work directly with the CEO, who is also based in the Bay Area.

  • Build the US community function from the start, with budget and a clear path to leading it.

jobs.title: Founding Customer Success Lead
jobs.descriptionHtml:
Why this role exists

SigNoz is an open source observability platform built on OpenTelemetry: logs, metrics and traces in one tool. It's designed for an era where agents and humans run observability together. We are a YC company with 32K+ GitHub stars, and revenue grew 4x in 2025.

Most of our revenue is usage-based. That makes customer success especially important: retaining accounts and helping our larger accounts expand drive a big share of our growth.

This is our first dedicated customer success role. We're looking for a builder who can design the systems from scratch and set them up to scale as the team grows. You'll work directly with the founders.

What you will own

1. Account coverage and health

  • Tier our paying accounts and decide what each tier gets: a named owner, a shared Slack channel, regular business reviews, or pooled coverage.

  • Build health scores from data we already have in our warehouse: ingestion volume, product usage, billing, support tickets and engagement.

  • Set up a review cadence for the top tier, and make sure each top account has several contacts on their side, not one champion.

2. Retention and save plays

  • Catch risk early. Usage drops, a champion leaving, a surprise bill and alerts going quiet are all signals. On a usage-based product, a billing spike can be as much of a churn risk as a usage drop.

  • Turn each signal into a play: who reaches out, what we offer (often help reducing their cost), and when it escalates.

  • Run a post-mortem on every meaningful churn or downgrade, and feed the lessons back into product, pricing and onboarding.

  • Run win-back campaigns for accounts we lost.

3. Annual commitments and expansion

  • Move monthly usage-based customers onto annual commitments, and own those conversations, including the commercial terms.

  • Spot expansion opportunities: new teams, new signals (logs, traces, metrics), new environments. Work with sales on the bigger ones.

  • Own renewals for customers on annual plans.

4. Voice of the customer

  • Bring what customers need back to product and engineering, ranked by revenue impact.

  • Work with our technical support team on escalations so the most important accounts never wait.

Across all of it

  • Agree retention targets with the founders, then own the gross and net revenue retention numbers.

  • Run a weekly account review: at-risk accounts, saves, annual conversions in progress, expansion.

How the role grows

This role starts hands-on. You will personally own our top accounts and build the playbooks by running them yourself. We are not looking for someone who needs a team before anything happens.

Build the systems so they keep working as the number of accounts grows: clear tiers, health scores the team trusts, and playbooks a new CSM can pick up and run. Once they're working, you build and lead the customer success team.

What success looks like

  • 30 days: You know the product and the data, and have met our top accounts. Account tiers and a first version of the health score are drafted.

  • 90 days: The health score is live and the team trusts it. Business reviews are running for the top tier. Save plays exist for usage drops and billing spikes, and every meaningful churn gets a post-mortem. The first monthly-to-annual conversions have closed.

  • 12 months: Gross and net revenue retention are measurably up, and a much larger share of revenue is on annual commitments. The systems you built are ready for the team to scale on.

Who we think fits

  • 6-10 years in B2B SaaS customer success, with at least part of that at a technical product sold to engineers.

  • You've owned a revenue retention number (GRR, NRR or renewals), not just CSAT or ticket metrics. You can walk us through accounts you saved and grew, and what you did.

  • You've worked with usage-based or consumption pricing, and you know how to talk to a customer whose bill just jumped.

  • You're a builder. You've set up CS systems from scratch (health scores, business reviews, playbooks) and made them work as the book of accounts grew. You didn't just inherit them.

  • You're technical enough to talk to SREs and platform engineers, read a usage dashboard, and write basic SQL, or you'll learn it fast.

  • You're commercial. You can negotiate an annual commitment and you're comfortable talking about money.

  • You've managed US-based customers directly: running their reviews, handling escalations and negotiating renewals. You can overlap with US mornings (India evenings) a few times a week.

  • You've led or mentored other CSMs. Formal management is a plus, not a requirement.

Bonus points

  • A background in engineering and can understand technical terms

  • You've set up a CS platform or built health scoring on raw data

  • You've moved customers from monthly to annual plans at scale

Why SigNoz

  • Customers who already love the product. Our customers chose us themselves. Your job is to keep that going as they grow, not to rescue bad deals.

  • Build the function from day one. You're the first dedicated CS hire, so you design how customer success works here and set it up to scale.

  • Work directly with the founders. You'll have the founders' backing, the data to work with, and a clear path to running the function.

  • A global dev-infra product, backed by YC and leading Bay Area VCs. Fully remote.
